chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said; al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayb, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in his sermon:

I am the Guide, and I am the Rightly-Guided, and I am the Father of the Orphans and the Poor, and the Husband of the Widows, and I am the Refuge of every weak one and the Shelter of every fearful one, and I am the Leader of the Believers to Paradise, and I am the Firm Rope of Allah, and I am the Firmest Handle of Allah and the Word of Piety, and I am the Eye of Allah, and His Truthful Tongue, and His Hand, and I am the Side of Allah who says: 'Lest a soul should say: O woe to me! For what I fell short of my duty to Allah,' and I am the Outspread Hand of Allah towards His Servants, granting mercy and forgiveness, and I am the Door of Divine Mercy. Whoever recognizes me and recognizes my right has recognized his Lord, because I am the Successor of my Prophet on His Earth, and His Proof upon His creation. No one denies this except one who rejects Allah and His Messenger.
Lest a soul should say: O woe to me! For what I fell short of my duty to Allah.

The Compiler of this book (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Al-Janb' (Side) in the language of the Arabs means obedience. It is said: 'This is little in the side of Allah,' meaning 'This is little in terms of obedience to Allah, the Mighty and High.' Therefore, the meaning of the statement of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'I am the Side of Allah,' is 'I am the one whose guardianship represents obedience to Allah.' Allah, the Mighty and High, said: 'Lest a soul should say: O woe to me! For what I fell short of my duty to Allah,' i.e., in the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and High.

key_terms.جَنْبُ اللَّهِ: The Side of Allah, interpreted here as obedience and Wilayah

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean when he says 'I am the Side of Allah'?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Tawhid highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) role as the 'Side of Allah' (Janb Allah), where Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies that 'Janb' signifies obedience, thereby linking Imamate directly to divine command. The text emphasizes that recognizing the Imam’s authority is equivalent to recognizing Allah, a concept rooted in the verse regarding regret for falling short in Allah's 'side' or obedience. This interpretation underscores the Shia doctrine of Wilayah as the practical manifestation of God's will on earth.
